blocks.prompt: 12. The acceleration of a particle is \(a(t) = \frac{1}{1 + t}\) for \(t \ge 0\). If the velocity is 0 m/s when \(t = 0\), find the velocity at \(t = 5\) seconds.
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein acceleration constant nahi, balke waqt ke saath badal raha hai (\(t\) barhe to \(a\) kam hota hai). Is liye \(v = u + at\) jaisi equations of motion yahan nahi chalengi; woh sirf constant acceleration ke liye hain.
Diya kya hai? \(a(t) = \frac{1}{1 + t}\) aur \(t = 0\) par \(v = 0\).
Find kya karna hai? \(t = 5\) s par velocity.
Rule kaunsa? \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\), is liye integration se velocity milegi, bilkul kitab ki Examples 9 aur 10 ki tarah.
Plan: integrate karein, initial condition se constant nikalein, phir \(t = 5\) rakhein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(a(t) = \frac{1}{1 + t}\), \(t \ge 0\), aur \(t = 0\) par \(v = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(t = 5\) s par velocity.
Tareeqa: Acceleration velocity ka rate of change hai, \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\). Rate se asal cheez wapas lane ke liye integrate karte hain, is liye \(a(t)\) ko \(t\) ke lehaz se integrate karenge. Integration ke saath constant \(c\) aata hai, jo initial condition (shuru ki halat) se maloom hoga.

Acceleration ko integrate karein
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{1 + t}\]
\[\int dv = \int \dfrac{1}{1 + t}\,dt\]
\[v(t) = \ln(1 + t) + c\]
Kyun: Yaad karein, \(\int \frac{1}{u}\,du = \ln|u|\). Yahan \(u = 1 + t\) hai aur \(du = dt\). \(t \ge 0\) hai to \(1 + t\) hamesha positive hai, is liye modulus ki zaroorat nahi.
Dhyan dein: Constant \(c\) likhna mat bhooliye; isi se initial condition ka faida uthaya jata hai.

Initial condition lagayein
\[0 = \ln(1 + 0) + c\]
\[0 = 0 + c \Rightarrow c = 0\]
\[v(t) = \ln(1 + t)\]
Kyun: \(t = 0\) par \(v = 0\) diya hai. \(\ln 1 = 0\) hota hai, kyunke \(e^0 = 1\). Is liye \(c = 0\) aaya aur velocity ka poora formula mil gaya.

t = 5 par velocity
\[v(5) = \ln(1 + 5) = \ln 6\]
\[v(5) \approx 1.79\ \text{m/s}\]
Kyun: Formula mein \(t = 5\) rakha. Calculator se \(\ln 6 \approx 1.7918\). Exact jawab \(\ln 6\) hai; decimal sirf andaza dene ke liye.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\ln(1 + t) = \dfrac{1}{1 + t}\ \checkmark\]
\[v(0) = \ln 1 = 0\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: Integration ka ulta differentiation hai. \(v(t)\) ko differentiate kiya to wapas diya hua \(a(t)\) mila, aur shuru ki shart bhi poori hui. Dono baatein sahi hain, is liye jawab sahi hai.
